title: Assessing VLM Reliability for Medical Image Quality Evaluation Under Corruption and Bias

bias_targets.methodology: Counterfactual name substitution and explicit demographic labels in text prompts (e.g., 'white doctor' vs. 'black doctor', and 'Dr. Tom Johnson' vs. 'Dr. Kwame Asante') alongside identical images to measure scoring disparities.

Modifying the described skill level and credentials of the image operator in the system prompt (e.g., 'world-renowned medical expert' vs. 'medical student') to measure its effect on image quality assessment.

Altering the stated equipment quality in the prompt (e.g., 'taken from a high-tech device' vs. 'taken from an old device') to test the model's sensitivity to equipment prestige independent of actual image quality.

Varying the stated institutional reputation in the text prompt (e.g., 'high world class medical institution' vs. 'local medical institution') to see if institutional prestige influences objective visual quality scores.
